citations.evidenceText:
Vanishing Gradient Problem & its solution
•  During Backpropagation (upcoming), gradients are multiplied layer by layer from
   the output back to the input.
•  The Core Issue: If we use Sigmoid or Tanh, the maximum gradient is small (e.g.,
  max gradient of Sigmoid is 0.25).
•  The Chain Effect: Multiplying many small numbers (say, 0.25*0.25*0.25…) causes
   the gradient to vanish or shrink to nearly zero as it reaches the earlier layers.
•  Impact on Robotics: The robot brain stops learning in its initial layers, meaning
     it cannot extract fundamental features from sensors
    effectively.
•  Solutions: ReLU (Rectified Linear Unit), Leaky ReLU,
  GELU (Gaussian Error Linear Unit)

Back Propagation
•  The goal of training an MLP is to minimize the loss function by adjusting the
   network's weights and biases, achieved through back propagation.
•   It is achieved through three key steps:
•  Step 1: Gradient Calculation
   – Calculate gradients of the loss function w.r.t. weights & bias
•  Step 2: Error Propagation
   – The error is propagated backwards through the network, layer by layer.
•  Step 3: Gradient Descent
   – The network updates the weights & biases by moving to the
    opposite direction of the gradient
    –  We’ll discuss in detail in the upcoming slides.
